constraints_observed.java_svg_generation: All six Java SVGs were generated with -Djava.awt.headless=true and validated with xmllint --noout. None contains a PlantUML syntax-error page.
constraints_observed.working_tree_note: The review started with HEAD 899d1edc. During the review another task advanced this shared isolated checkout to 5635cb2e and left direction-related Rust edits unstaged. Those files were not staged or edited by the checker. The requested prebuilt helper was used without rebuilding; its recorded hash is the executable identity used for every comparison.

java_findings: StripeSimple#getAtoms inserts AtomTextUtils.createLegacy(" ", fontConfiguration) when a logical row has no atoms.
CreoleParser#createSheetSlow sends each Display row, including empty rows, through createStripes and adds the resulting stripe to the Sheet.

SheetBlock1#initMap measures each retained stripe, advances the row stack by its height, aligns it within the maximum width, and drawU emits the same atom positions. The Java behavior is therefore a row-level atom invariant, not a fixture-specific width constant.
rust_findings: Commit 899d1edc adds StateTransitionLabelBlock#paint_row, mapping only empty logical rows to one ordinary space before width, height, baseline, emission, and painted-y calculations.

The three top-to-bottom cases confirm that the empty atom is retained through measurement and SVG emission: Java and Rust both emit positive-width   text nodes for empty first, intermediate, and final rows.

The two non-Times LR cases also report matching positive empty-row widths, but the overall diagrams are laid out vertically by Rust instead of horizontally. This is the pre-existing LR/state layout residue identified by the parent rejecting review, not evidence that the empty atom disappeared.

The Times New Roman LR case has a separate font-metric mismatch: Java reports 3.75 for the empty row while Rust reports 4.7461, and the non-empty rows also differ (for example begin is 33.3252 versus 40.7959). The failure cannot be assigned specifically to empty-row materialization.

overfit_scan.constants: The only mechanism-specific new literal is the Java-cited ordinary-space atom in paint_row. No coordinate ladder, per-branch-count constant, or unexplained parity-affecting numeric constant was found in commit 899d1edc.
overfit_scan.pre_existing_scope: The broader renderer contains pre-existing oracle/captured-golden paths and tests; those were not attributed to this commit and were not used as evidence for acceptance.

summary.empty_row_atom_isolated_result: The fix survives the three top-to-bottom cases covering empty first, intermediate, and final rows, plus self and pseudostate endpoints, and the empty-row widths match in two of three LR cases. No isolated counterexample to the ordinary-space atom normalization was found.
summary.primary_reject_reason: The held-out matrix includes the account's declared left-to-right and font axes, and three valid cases fail the no-oracle comparator. Two fail through known LR/state layout residue; one additionally exposes an existing Times New Roman metrics mismatch. The parity gate requires the full mechanism-shaped perturbation matrix to pass, so the implementation cannot be accepted.
residue: left-to-right state/autonomous layout remains vertical in Rust for the fresh ordinary, nested, and pseudostate cases
Times New Roman metrics differ for both empty and non-empty rows
summary.recommendation: Keep all six failing or passing pairs preserved. Do not alter comparator slack or park these failures. Address LR layout and font-family metrics as separate causal mechanisms before a later empty-row review claims the full declared perturbation axes are green.
